WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: Warehouse load date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse; constant '20-DEC-24' in this snapshot.

table.name: TIME_DAY
table.purpose: Date dimension table for a data warehouse: one row per calendar day (10,000 days, ~1950-2035), with attributes mapping each date to calendar month, MIT fiscal year/period (fiscal year appears to run July-June, so FY = calendar year + 1 for months Jul-Dec), academic term/year, and financial aid year. Used to join time-based facts to academic, fiscal, and financial-aid time frames. Related to TIME_MONTH and TIME_QUARTER tables in the same warehouse.

ACADEMIC_TERM_CODE.name: academic_term_code
ACADEMIC_TERM_CODE.description: Code of the academic term the date falls in, e.g. 2005SP = Spring Term 2004-2005, 2016SU = Summer 2016, 2008FA = Fall 2008. Null for dates outside academic terms (e.g. summer/winter breaks). References ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL.

ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION.name: academic_term_description
ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable label of the academic term, e.g. 'Spring Term 2004-2005', 'Summer Term 1952'. Null when ACADEMIC_TERM_CODE is null.

ACADEMIC_YEAR.name: academic_year
ACADEMIC_YEAR.description: Ending calendar year of the academic year the date belongs to (e.g. 2005 for Spring Term 2004-2005). Null outside academic terms.

CALENDAR_DATE.name: calendar_date
CALENDAR_DATE.description: The calendar date of the row, in DD-MON-YY Oracle format (e.g. 04-FEB-05). Unique per row; the grain of the table.

CALENDAR_PERIOD.name: calendar_period
CALENDAR_PERIOD.description: Calendar month as YYYYMM integer, e.g. 200502 = February 2005.

DAY_OF_WEEK.name: day_of_week
DAY_OF_WEEK.description: Day-of-week name of the date (padded to fixed width, e.g. 'Friday   ').

END_DATE.name: end_date
END_DATE.description: Last day of the calendar month containing the date, DD-MON-YY format (e.g. 28-FEB-05).

FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR.name: financial_aid_year
FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR.description: Ending year of the financial aid award year the date falls in (aid years run like academic years, e.g. 2005 = Aid Year 2004-2005). Only populated from 1994 onward; null for earlier dates and some non-term dates.

FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC.name: financial_aid_year_desc
FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC.description: Human-readable financial aid year label, e.g. 'Aid Year 2004-2005', 'Aid Year 1998-99'.

FISCAL_PERIOD.name: fiscal_period
FISCAL_PERIOD.description: Fiscal accounting period as YYYYPP, where PP is the period (month) within the fiscal year. Fiscal year appears to start in July (e.g. Sep 1960 -> 196103), so FY = calendar year + 1 for months July-December.

FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.name: fiscal_period_description
FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable fiscal period label, e.g. 'FY 2005 Period 8'.

FISCAL_YEAR.name: fiscal_year
FISCAL_YEAR.description: Fiscal year of the date (July-June fiscal year; e.g. 24-SEP-60 belongs to FY 1961).

START_DATE.name: start_date
START_DATE.description: First day of the calendar month containing the date, DD-MON-YY format (e.g. 01-FEB-05).

table.name: TIME_MONTH
table.purpose: A date/time dimension table in a data warehouse (MIT context, given other tables). One row per fiscal period (month) from FY1996 through FY2035, mapping each calendar month to MIT's July-June fiscal year, fiscal period number, fiscal quarter, academic term/year, and financial aid year. Includes closing periods (periods 13-16) and flags for the current/previous fiscal period and year. Referenced by facility history tables and fiscal period tables as the time key.

ACADEMIC_TERM.name: academic_term_code
ACADEMIC_TERM.description: Code for the academic term the month falls in, e.g. 2000FA (Fall), 2022SP (Spring), 2028SU (Summer), 2001JA (January/IAP). References ACADEMIC_TERMS. Null when the month falls outside any academic term (e.g. summer closing months).

ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION.name: academic_term_description
ACADEMIC_TERM_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable form of ACADEMIC_TERM, e.g. 'Fall Term 1999-2000', 'Summer Term 2028'. Nulls match ACADEMIC_TERM.

ACADEMIC_YEAR.name: academic_year
ACADEMIC_YEAR.description: Ending calendar year of the academic year the month belongs to (e.g. 2000 for Fall Term 1999-2000). Null when no academic term applies.

CALENDAR_MONTH.name: calendar_month_number
CALENDAR_MONTH.description: Calendar month number 1-12 of the period.

CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME.name: calendar_month_name
CALENDAR_MONTH_NAME.description: Name of the calendar month, e.g. 'June', 'November'.

CALENDAR_PERIOD.name: calendar_period_code
CALENDAR_PERIOD.description: Unique code for the calendar month, YYYYMM (e.g. 199911); closing periods get a suffix like '202806P16' for June 2028 fiscal period 16.

CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.name: calendar_period_description
CALENDAR_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable calendar period, e.g. 'November 1999', 'June 2028, fiscal period 16'.

END_DATE.name: period_end_date
END_DATE.description: Last calendar date of the month, in DD-MON-YY Oracle format (e.g. '30-NOV-99', '28-FEB-22').

FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR.name: financial_aid_year
FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR.description: Starting year of the financial aid award year the month belongs to (aid year runs like 1999-2000, coded as 2000 here per FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC 'Aid Year 1999-2000' -> 2000). Null for months outside the aid year (e.g. summer closing months).

FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC.name: financial_aid_year_description
FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR_DESC.description: Human-readable aid year, e.g. 'Aid Year 1999-2000'. Nulls match FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR.

FISCAL_PERIOD.name: fiscal_period_code
FISCAL_PERIOD.description: Fiscal period key, YYYYNN where YYYY is the fiscal year (ending) and NN the period number (1-12 for months July-June, 13-16 for closing periods). E.g. 200005 = FY2000 period 5 = November 1999. Referenced by facility history tables and TIME_QUARTER.

FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.name: fiscal_period_description
FISCAL_PERIOD_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable fiscal period, e.g. 'FY 2000 Period 5', 'FY 2028 closing period 4'.

FISCAL_PERIOD_SELECTOR.name: fiscal_period_selector
FISCAL_PERIOD_SELECTOR.description: Display/selector string combining code and month, e.g. '200005 -- November 1999', '201215 -- June 2012 Closing'.

FISCAL_YEAR.name: fiscal_year
FISCAL_YEAR.description: Fiscal year (July-June, labeled by ending year), 1996-2035.

FISCAL_YEAR_QUARTER.name: fiscal_year_quarter_name
FISCAL_YEAR_QUARTER.description: Human-readable fiscal quarter, e.g. 'FY 2000 Quarter 2'. References TIME_QUARTER.FY_QUARTER_NAME.

FY_QUARTER_CODE.name: fiscal_quarter_code
FY_QUARTER_CODE.description: Compact fiscal quarter code, e.g. 'FY2000Q2'. References TIME_QUARTER.FY_QUARTER_CODE.

IS_CLOSING_PERIOD.name: is_closing_period
IS_CLOSING_PERIOD.description: Y/N flag: Y for fiscal closing periods (13-16, the June closing months), N for regular monthly periods.

IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD.name: is_current_fiscal_period
IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_PERIOD.description: Y/N flag: Y for the single row representing the current fiscal period as of the data snapshot.

IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_YEAR.name: is_current_fiscal_year
IS_CURRENT_FISCAL_YEAR.description: Y/N flag: Y for the 16 rows of the current fiscal year as of the data snapshot.

IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD.name: is_previous_fiscal_period
IS_PREVIOUS_FISCAL_PERIOD.description: Y/N flag: Y for the single row representing the immediately preceding fiscal period.

START_DATE.name: period_start_date
START_DATE.description: First calendar date of the month, in DD-MON-YY Oracle format (e.g. '01-NOV-99').

TIME_MONTH_KEY.name: time_month_key
TIME_MONTH_KEY.description: Primary key of the table (surrogate/primary identifier), identical to FISCAL_PERIOD (YYYYNN). Referenced by FRC_FISCAL_PERIODS, facility history tables, and TIME_QUARTER start/end period columns.

table.name: TIME_QUARTER
table.purpose: Time dimension table of fiscal and calendar quarters (one row per quarter, FY2000Q1 through FY2035Q4, 144 rows). MIT's fiscal year runs July 1 - June 30, so fiscal quarters map to calendar quarters offset by two quarters (e.g., FY2004Q2 = CY2003Q4). Also carries payroll/effort-certification (ED/ACCA) quarterly schedule dates. Referenced by TIME_MONTH, which rolls months up to quarters.

CALENDAR_YEAR.name: calendar_year
CALENDAR_YEAR.description: Calendar year (Gregorian) in which the quarter falls, e.g. 2003. Each year appears 4 times (one per quarter).

CY_QUARTER_CODE.name: calendar_quarter_code
CY_QUARTER_CODE.description: Unique code for the calendar quarter, format CY<year>Q<1-4>, e.g. CY2003Q4.

CY_QUARTER_NAME.name: calendar_quarter_name
CY_QUARTER_NAME.description: Human-readable calendar quarter label, e.g. 'CY 2003 Quarter 4'.

FISCAL_YEAR.name: fiscal_year
FISCAL_YEAR.description: Fiscal year (July-June) the quarter belongs to. Calendar Q3/Q4 belong to the following fiscal year (CY2003Q4 -> FY2004).

FY_QUARTER_CODE.name: fiscal_quarter_code
FY_QUARTER_CODE.description: Primary key. Unique fiscal quarter code, format FY<year>Q<1-4>, e.g. FY2004Q2. Referenced by TIME_MONTH.FY_QUARTER_CODE.

FY_QUARTER_NAME.name: fiscal_quarter_name
FY_QUARTER_NAME.description: Human-readable fiscal quarter label, e.g. 'FY 2004 Quarter 2'.

IS_CURRENT_QUARTER.name: is_current_quarter
IS_CURRENT_QUARTER.description: Y/N flag: whether this quarter is the current quarter as of the warehouse load (exactly one row is Y).

IS_FUTURE_QUARTER.name: is_future_quarter
IS_FUTURE_QUARTER.description: Y/N flag: whether the quarter is in the future relative to the load date (42 rows Y).

IS_NEXT_QUARTER.name: is_next_quarter
IS_NEXT_QUARTER.description: Y/N flag: whether this is the quarter immediately following the current one. All rows are N in this snapshot (the next quarter likely falls outside the loaded range or the flag was not populated).

IS_PAST_QUARTER.name: is_past_quarter
IS_PAST_QUARTER.description: Y/N flag: whether the quarter is in the past relative to the load date (101 rows Y).

IS_PREVIOUS_QUARTER.name: is_previous_quarter
IS_PREVIOUS_QUARTER.description: Y/N flag: whether this is the quarter immediately before the current one. All rows are N in this snapshot.

PAYROLL_EDACCA_CERT_SCHED_KEY.name: payroll_edacca_cert_schedule_key
PAYROLL_EDACCA_CERT_SCHED_KEY.description: Key for the payroll effort-certification (ED/ACCA) quarterly schedule, format YYYYQQ (fiscal year + fiscal quarter number), e.g. 200402 for FY2004 Q2. Matches QUARTER_START_FP.

QUARTER_CERT_DUE.name: quarter_cert_due_date
QUARTER_CERT_DUE.description: Due date for the quarterly effort certification, DD-MON-YY; falls about a month after quarter end (e.g. 31-MAR-04 for the Oct-Dec 2003 quarter).

QUARTER_CERT_EXPECTED.name: quarter_cert_expected_date
QUARTER_CERT_EXPECTED.description: Expected return date for the quarterly effort certification, DD-MON-YY; end of the month following quarter end (e.g. 29-FEB-04).

QUARTER_CERT_OPEN.name: quarter_cert_open_date
QUARTER_CERT_OPEN.description: Date the quarterly certification period opens, DD-MON-YY; equals the quarter start date (e.g. 01-JAN-04).

QUARTER_END_DATE.name: quarter_end_date
QUARTER_END_DATE.description: Last calendar date of the quarter, DD-MON-YY (e.g. 31-DEC-03).

QUARTER_END_FP.name: quarter_end_fiscal_period
QUARTER_END_FP.description: Fiscal period (YYYYMM) of the last month in the quarter, e.g. 200406 for the quarter ending Dec 2003 (fiscal period numbering continues July=01). Joins to TIME_MONTH fiscal period keys.

QUARTER_START_DATE.name: quarter_start_date
QUARTER_START_DATE.description: First calendar date of the quarter, DD-MON-YY (e.g. 01-OCT-03).

QUARTER_START_FP.name: quarter_start_fiscal_period
QUARTER_START_FP.description: Fiscal period (YYYYMM) of the first month in the quarter, e.g. 200404 for the quarter starting Oct 2003. Joins to TIME_MONTH fiscal period keys.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse; constant 20-DEC-24 for all rows in this snapshot.

table.name: TIP_DETAIL
table.purpose: Textbook/material detail per course offering per term in MIT's Textbook Information Project (TIP): one row per course material (or 'no materials' record) for a subject offered in a given academic term, with ISBN and material status codes. Joins to TIP_MATERIAL, TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS, TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED and ACADEMIC_TERMS by embedded keys/term codes.

ISBN.name: ISBN
ISBN.description: ISBN of the course material (mostly ISBN-13, some ISBN-10). '0' and blank values mean no ISBN (e.g., non-book materials or no-material records); 22.5% null.

RECORD_COUNT.name: RECORD_COUNT
RECORD_COUNT.description: Constant 1 in every row; a per-row count used for aggregation (e.g., SUM(RECORD_COUNT) in BI tools).

SUBJECT_ID.name: SUBJECT_ID
SUBJECT_ID.description: MIT subject/course number (e.g., 21L.003, 14.781). Values like 'CANC.BARCHARTS'/'CANC.SPO' appear to be cancelled or special placeholder subjects.

TERM_CODE.name: TERM_CODE
TERM_CODE.description: Academic term code (YYYY + FA/SP/SU/JA for fall/spring/summer/IAP), referencing ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE.

TIP_MATERIAL_KEY.name: TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
TIP_MATERIAL_KEY.description: Composite key for the TIP_MATERIAL table: concatenation of ISBN (or 'N/A'), material title, edition and term code. 'N/A...Course has no materials...' rows are placeholder keys for courses without materials.

TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY.name: TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY.description: Code for the material's status, referencing TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS: RQ (required), RC (recommended), EO (optional/extra), NM (course has no materials), BR (bookstore recommends), CL (go to class first), U (unknown), NL (null).

TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY.name: TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY.description: Composite key for TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED: subject number (dots removed, zero-padded) + section/level digits + term code, e.g. 0173910002016FA for subject 17.391 in 2016FA.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: ETL load date of the row into the warehouse; constant '20-DEC-24' for this snapshot.

table.name: TIP_MATERIAL
table.purpose: One row per course material (textbook/book/other item) offered through the MIT Coop textbook program (TIP = Textbook/Tradebook Information Program, likely the Coop's textbook information service). Each row describes a book by ISBN/title/author/publisher with its new and used shelf prices and rental prices, keyed by a composite of ISBN + title + edition + term (e.g. '...142021SP' = 2021 spring). The same book can appear for multiple terms, hence the key embeds a term suffix. Related tables TIP_DETAIL, TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS, TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED carry the per-term/per-subject detail and status.

AUTHOR.name: author
AUTHOR.description: Author(s) of the book, in 'Last, First' catalog form, sometimes multiple authors separated by semicolons. Placeholder values like 'NOT FOUND on ISBN.org' and 'Unknown' occur when the author could not be determined.

EDITION.name: edition
EDITION.description: Edition number of the book, mostly a plain number ('2', '3') but sometimes with a year ('2nd 98', '2nd 97') or other text; heavily null and padded with spaces.

ISBN.name: isbn
ISBN.description: ISBN (13-digit form, e.g. 978...) identifying the book. 0 or blank means unknown/missing ISBN. Stored as text despite numeric appearance.

MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE.name: material_info_source
MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE.description: Code for where the material's metadata came from: 'ISBN' (looked up from ISBN.org), 'COOP' (MIT Coop), 'OTI' (another source, likely an online textbook vendor; exact expansion unresolved).

NEW_SHELF_PRICE.name: new_shelf_price_usd
NEW_SHELF_PRICE.description: Shelf price in whole US dollars for a new copy of the book.

PUBLISHER.name: publisher
PUBLISHER.description: Publisher of the book. Values are inconsistent: sometimes a publisher name, sometimes a full imprint/publication statement ('New York, Wiley [1975]'), sometimes abbreviated vendor names ('Vst', 'Yuzu', 'Dgtl Bncom' = digital bookstore/VitalSource/Yuzu/Digital Bookshelf).

RENTAL_NEW_PRICE.name: rental_new_price_usd
RENTAL_NEW_PRICE.description: Rental price in whole US dollars for a new copy; 0 (92% of rows) means the book is not offered for new-copy rental.

RENTAL_USED_PRICE.name: rental_used_price_usd
RENTAL_USED_PRICE.description: Rental price in whole US dollars for a used copy; 0 (92% of rows) means the book is not offered for used-copy rental.

TIP_MATERIAL_KEY.name: tip_material_key
TIP_MATERIAL_KEY.description: Primary key: concatenation of ISBN + abbreviated title + edition/year + term code (e.g. '142021SP' = spring 2021, '132013FA' = fall 2013). Identifies a specific book offered in a specific term.

TITLE.name: title
TITLE.description: Title of the book/material; some entries prefixed 'Ebk' indicating an e-book version.

USED_SHELF_PRICE.name: used_shelf_price_usd
USED_SHELF_PRICE.description: Shelf price in whole US dollars for a used copy; 0 means no used copy offered.

YEAR.name: publication_year
YEAR.description: Publication year of the book (1900s-2024); 0 or null means unknown.

table.name: TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
table.purpose: Lookup table of material status codes for TIP (Textbook/Teaching material Information Program?) course materials, e.g. Required, Recommended, etc. Referenced by TIP_DETAIL rows describing individual course materials. Analogous to LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS.

TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS.name: material_status_description
TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS.description: Human-readable description of the material status (e.g. 'Required', 'Recommended', 'Bookstore recommends', 'Course has no materials', 'Go to class first', 'Val-u option'). Null for some codes (e.g. 'NL'), so not all codes have a label.

TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE.name: material_status_code
TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE.description: Two-letter abbreviation code for the material status (BR = Bookstore recommends, NM = Course has no materials, etc.). Duplicates the key column.

TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY.name: material_status_key
TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY.description: Primary key of the lookup; two-letter code joined to TIP_DETAIL.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY to classify each course material's status.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse (all rows '20-DEC-24'); stored as text in DD-MON-YY format.

table.name: TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED
table.purpose: Fact table of MIT subject (course) offerings per academic term, as used by the TIP (Teaching/Instructor Photo or course-materials) process: one row per subject offered in a term, with the offering department, school, responsible faculty member, enrollment count, and the master (cross-listed) subject it maps to. Grain is subject x term, keyed by TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY (subject id zero-padded + term code).

COURSE_NUMBER.name: offering_course_number
COURSE_NUMBER.description: MIT course (department) number of the subject as offered, e.g. '15' = Management, '6' = EECS, '21M' = Music and Theater Arts. References SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.COURSE_NUMBER.

COURSE_NUMBER_DESC.name: offering_course_number_description
COURSE_NUMBER_DESC.description: Human-readable name of the course/department number, e.g. '15' -> 'Management', '21M' -> 'Music and Theater Arts'.

COURSE_NUMBER_SORT.name: offering_course_number_sort_key
COURSE_NUMBER_SORT.description: Course number padded with leading spaces (numeric codes) so numeric and alphanumeric course numbers sort correctly; same domain as COURSE_NUMBER.

IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL.name: no_course_material_flag
IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL.description: Y/N flag indicating whether the subject offering has no course material (e.g. no reading/reserve material to collect for TIP). Null (79%) likely means not applicable or not evaluated; the Y/N semantics are plausible but the exact business rule is not directly evidenced, and no joined column provides further support.

MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER.name: master_course_number
MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER.description: Course number of the master (primary/cross-listed parent) subject; usually equals COURSE_NUMBER but differs for cross-listed subjects. References SIS_SUBJECT_CODE.COURSE_NUMBER.

MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_DESC.name: master_course_number_description
MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER_DESC.description: Human-readable name of the master course number's department.

MASTER_SUBJECT_ID.name: master_subject_id
MASTER_SUBJECT_ID.description: Full master subject identifier (course.number, e.g. '2.EPE', '15.792') of the primary subject this offering rolls up to; differs from SUBJECT_ID for cross-listed subjects.

NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS.name: enrolled_student_count
NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS.description: Number of students enrolled in the subject offering that term (0-648, median 5).

OFFER_DEPT_CODE.name: offering_department_code
OFFER_DEPT_CODE.description: Code of the department offering the subject; nearly identical to COURSE_NUMBER (62 vs 58 distinct values, e.g. '21M' vs 'Music').

OFFER_DEPT_NAME.name: offering_department_name
OFFER_DEPT_NAME.description: Name of the offering department, e.g. 'Music' (finer-grained than COURSE_NUMBER_DESC, which groups departments into course numbers).

OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME.name: offering_school_name
OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME.description: MIT school the offering department belongs to: Engineering, Science, Hum Arts & Social Sciences, Architecture and Planning, Sloan Management, etc.

RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID.name: responsible_faculty_mit_id
RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID.description: MIT ID number of the faculty member responsible for the subject offering; null for ~17% of rows (no assigned responsible faculty).

RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME.name: responsible_faculty_name
RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME.description: Name (Last, First) of the responsible faculty member, matching RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID.

SUBJECT_ID.name: subject_id
SUBJECT_ID.description: Full subject identifier of the offering, e.g. '21M.835', '15.220' (course number + subject number).

SUBJECT_ID_SORT.name: subject_id_sort_key
SUBJECT_ID_SORT.description: Space-padded sort key for SUBJECT_ID so numeric course numbers sort before alphanumeric ones.

SUBJECT_TITLE.name: subject_title
SUBJECT_TITLE.description: Title of the subject, e.g. 'Acting Techniques of Style', 'International Management'.

TERM_CODE.name: term_code
TERM_CODE.description: Academic term of the offering in YYYY+session format (FA fall, SP spring, SU summer, JA January/IAP), e.g. 2019FA. References ACADEMIC_TERMS.TERM_CODE.

TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY.name: tip_subject_offered_key
TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY.description: Primary key: subject id zero-padded to 9 chars concatenated with term code, e.g. '21M8350002002FA' = subject 21M.835 in 2002FA.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse; constant '20-DEC-24' for this extract.

table.name: TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN
table.purpose: Lookup table of Internet top-level domains (mostly ISO 3166-1 two-letter country codes plus a few special/generic TLDs like ARPA), each with a human-readable description (usually the country name). Loaded into the MIT data warehouse in June 1999, likely used to decode country codes in email/web addresses or person records.

TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN.name: top_level_domain_code
TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN.description: The top-level domain code itself, e.g. 'HU', 'KG', 'SB', 'ARPA'. Nearly unique (one null); duplicates TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN_KEY.

TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN_DESCRIPTION.name: top_level_domain_description
TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN_DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable label for the TLD code — the country name (e.g. 'Hungary', 'Kyrgzstan', 'Solomon Islands') or, for special TLDs, an expansion (e.g. 'Advanced Projects Research Agency' for ARPA).

TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN_KEY.name: top_level_domain_key
TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN_KEY.description: Primary/lookup key of the table; identical in content to TOP_LEVEL_DOMAIN (e.g. 'HU', 'ARPA'). One null row.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the warehouse, in Oracle DD-MON-YY format; 248 rows loaded 17-JUN-99, one row 21-JUN-99.

table.name: WAREHOUSE_USERS
table.purpose: Directory of MIT warehouse/data-warehouse users: one row per person (employee or student) with their MIT ID, Kerberos username, names, contact info, and home organizational unit. Appears to be a person directory snapshot, likely sourced from MIT's data warehouse (roles/warehouse access population).

APPOINTMENT_TYPE.name: appointment_type
APPOINTMENT_TYPE.description: Type of appointment; only value observed is 'Primary Appointment', indicating the row reflects the person's primary MIT appointment.

EMAIL_ADDRESS.name: email_address
EMAIL_ADDRESS.description: Person's email address (synthetic/anonymized domains like worker.com, employee.com). Not unique; some addresses shared by multiple rows.

KRB_NAME.name: kerberos_username
KRB_NAME.description: MIT Kerberos/Athena username (lowercase), typically firstname + last initial.

KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE.name: kerberos_username_uppercase
KRB_NAME_UPPERCASE.description: Same Kerberos username in uppercase; some values include a numeric suffix (e.g., CHADN7), likely disambiguation for duplicate names.

MIDDLE_NAME.name: middle_name
MIDDLE_NAME.description: Person's middle name or middle initial; null for about half the rows.

MIT_ID.name: mit_id
MIT_ID.description: MIT personal identification number, 9-digit (900000000-999999999 range); unique, primary key of the table.

OFFICE_LOCATION.name: office_location
OFFICE_LOCATION.description: Office location in MIT building-room format (e.g., E53-355, 5-172F, NE49); building number optionally followed by room. Null for ~11%.

OFFICE_PHONE.name: office_phone
OFFICE_PHONE.description: Office phone number stored as digits (anonymized/synthetic values, 5-10 digits). Null for ~17%.

UNIT_ID.name: unit_id
UNIT_ID.description: Identifier of the person's home MIT organizational unit (6-digit DLC code, e.g., 310000 = Lincoln Laboratory). Pairs with UNIT_NAME.

UNIT_NAME.name: unit_name
UNIT_NAME.description: Name of the person's home MIT organizational unit (department, lab, or center), e.g., 'Lincoln Laboratory', 'Mechanical Engineering'.

YEAR.name: year
YEAR.description: Almost entirely null; only values 'G' (20) and '1' (3). Possibly a student class year ('G' = graduate, '1' = freshman) populated only for the STUDENT rows, but evidence is too sparse to confirm.

table.name: ZIP_CANADA
table.purpose: Canadian postal code lookup table; this extract contains only Newfoundland (NL) postal codes mapped to city names. Companion to ZIP_USA. Each row is one postal code (or a small number of duplicate rows) with its city and province. Likely used to validate/standardize Canadian addresses in the MIT data warehouse context.

CITY_NAME.name: city_name
CITY_NAME.description: Name of the Canadian city/locality for the postal code (e.g. St. John's, Corner Brook).

CITY_TYPE.name: city_type
CITY_TYPE.description: Code distinguishing city types; 'D' (dominant, 99.9%) vs 'A' (alternate, 0.1%). Likely marks whether the city name is the primary/official name for the postal code or an alternate/acceptable name. Exact code definitions are not documented, so this reading is plausible but unconfirmed.

POSTAL_CODE.name: postal_code
POSTAL_CODE.description: Canadian postal code in 'A1A 1A5' format (letter-digit-letter digit-letter-digit). Primary key of the table.

PROVINCE_ABBR.name: province_abbreviation
PROVINCE_ABBR.description: Two-letter Canadian province/territory abbreviation; all rows in this extract are 'NL' (Newfoundland and Labrador).

PROVINCE_NAME.name: province_name
PROVINCE_NAME.description: Full province name; all rows are 'Newfoundland' (the historical name for Newfoundland and Labrador).

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse, in DD-MON-YY format; all rows loaded 25-MAY-23.

table.name: ZIP_USA
table.purpose: US postal ZIP code reference table: one row per ZIP code (or ZIP prefix) with its city, county, and state. Note: values appear truncated to 4 digits (e.g. 715, 5149), suggesting leading zeros were lost or codes are stored as numeric prefixes; coverage is limited to ~11 states/territories (PR, NJ, MA, ME, VT, RI, NY, VI, AE, etc.).

CITY_NAME.name: city_name
CITY_NAME.description: Name of the city, town, or postal community served by the ZIP code. Includes military addresses (APO/DPO/FPO) and urbanization names in Puerto Rico ('Urb ...').

CITY_TYPE.name: city_type
CITY_TYPE.description: Code classifying the place type. Values N, D, A. Likely N = non-incorporated community, D = incorporated (default) place, A = APO/military or alternate name; exact code meanings are not documented, so specific mapping is tentative.

COUNTY_NAME.name: county_name
COUNTY_NAME.description: County (or municipio in Puerto Rico) containing the ZIP code; 'none' where no county applies (e.g. military/APO).

STATE_ABBR.name: state_abbr
STATE_ABBR.description: Two-letter USPS state/territory abbreviation (PR, NJ, MA, ME, VT, RI, NY, VI, AE for Armed Forces Europe, etc.).

STATE_NAME.name: state_name
STATE_NAME.description: Full name of the state or territory corresponding to STATE_ABBR.

WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.name: warehouse_load_date
WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.description: Date the row was loaded into the data warehouse; constant '25-MAY-23' for all rows in this snapshot.

ZIP_CODE.name: zip_code
ZIP_CODE.description: US ZIP code for the row. Stored as a number, so leading zeros are lost (e.g. 715 = 00715 Ponce PR, 926 = 00926 San Juan PR); values are 3-5 digit ZIP codes. Not unique — a ZIP can have multiple rows (e.g. multiple city/county names).

ZIP_TYPE.name: zip_type
ZIP_TYPE.description: Code classifying the ZIP record. S = standard ZIP (dominant), P = PO Box ZIP, U = unique (single high-volume recipient), M = military. Exact USPS code meanings inferred from standard conventions.

table.name: ZPM_ROOMS_LOAD
table.purpose: A facilities/space-management extract listing MIT rooms with their building component, floor, room number, space usage classification, owning organizational unit, and an access/security level. Likely a load table feeding a space or room-tracking system (ZPM suggests a SAP PM plant-maintenance-style module). Each row is one room/space record.

ACCESS_LEVEL.name: ACCESS_LEVEL
ACCESS_LEVEL.description: Coded access/security level of the room, values 0-3. Exact meaning of each level is not documented here; 2 is most common. Could alternatively be a key-card access tier or a room-lock classification.

BUILDING_COMPONENT.name: BUILDING_COMPONENT
BUILDING_COMPONENT.description: Building number (MIT building code), e.g. 10, 13, 32, 36; some values like '42T' indicate sub-building/wing codes. Part of the room identifier.

BUILDING_ROOM.name: BUILDING_ROOM
BUILDING_ROOM.description: Full room identifier in MIT 'building-room' format, e.g. '10-409', '32-G404H' (G = ground floor). Nearly unique per row; combined with building component it identifies the room.

FLOOR.name: FLOOR
FLOOR.description: Floor code within the building; numeric floors ('0'-'4'...) plus basement/sub-level codes like 'D6', 'D7', 'G6'. References SPACE_FLOOR lookup for floor names.

HR_ORG_UNIT_ID.name: HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
HR_ORG_UNIT_ID.description: ID of the HR organizational unit responsible for/occupying the room; references HR_ORG_UNIT and HR_ORG_UNIT_NEW.

SPACE_UNIT_CODE.name: SPACE_UNIT_CODE
SPACE_UNIT_CODE.description: Space accounting unit code (DLC/department space charge code) that owns or occupies the room; references SPACE_UNIT.

SPACE_USAGE.name: SPACE_USAGE
SPACE_USAGE.description: Space use classification code (abbreviated), e.g. STF ROOM (staff room), RESEARCH CENTER, IT HLPDSK (IT help desk), SLS OFFICE (sales office), FIL RM (file room), RSRC RM (resource room), TRNG RM (training room).
